content.text: No arbitration provision exists anywhere; the clause sits squarely at the preferred position.

input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects New York law (with a CISG disclaimer) and Section 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and a venue-objection waiver. This is exactly the playbook's preferred position: an accepted governing law plus court venue rather than arbitration. No arbitration provision appears anywhere in the document, so there is no foreign seat concern. The carve-out in 28.2 permitting temporary injunctive relief elsewhere is mutual and preserves our ability to protect confidential information and IP, and the pre-suit executive escalation in 28.3 is mutual, time-limited to fifteen business days, and expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings. No redline required.
